claim_ceiling: Finite-dimensional operator spreading under a declared U(1)-conserving random circuit. Squared commutators quantify operator influence for the chosen probes; they do not demonstrate message recovery, efficient decoding, black-hole evaporation, or thermalization.

model.initial_operator: Pauli X at site 2, identity on all other sites
model.circuit: nearest-neighbour 1D brickwork with independent Haar U(1) x U(2) x U(1) two-qubit gates
model.operator_convention: O <- U O U^dagger in circuit application order

independent_numpy_comparator.implementation: full 2^N x 2^N complex operator matrices, explicit embedded local U(1) gates, dense matrix conjugation O <- U O U^dagger, Frobenius commutators and normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm
independent_numpy_comparator.caveat: Independent NumPy PRNG and QR gate implementation. These are ensemble comparators, not bitwise outputs for the Rust ChaCha20 sequence.

interpretation: At depth zero, the local X operator anticommutes with Z at its source (normalized C_Z=2), and commutes with all other local X/Z probes.
Under the U(1)-conserving brickwork circuit, the probe commutator profiles spread across the chain while the operator Hilbert-Schmidt norm remains conserved.
This provides an independent operator-growth measurement alongside state entanglement entropy and domain-wall charge transport.
The six-site, 16-seed comparator is not an asymptotic front-velocity or thermalization result.
required_next_step: Extend to independent size/depth/seed sweeps and compare the operator front to charge-density hydrodynamics; do not infer recovery or decoder efficiency from OTOCs alone.
